messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT detected: KV cache working set spike + continuous-batching pack starvation. Metrics: kv_cache_size up 4x, batch_queue_depth rising, p99 latency jump on /v1/generate. Auto-triage tag: kv-cache, continuous-batching, scheduler
sre-oncall: Paging in. I’m on it, taking lead.
anika: Oncall here. Seeing a cluster-wide increase in KV evictions and paging. Affected GPUs: pool-phi-3 across us-west.
mike: Noted. Error rate on text-gen increased ~6% in last 10m, p95->p99 tail from 600ms -> 3.2s. Some requests stuck in batching for >2s.
tara: Any recent deploys touching batching or prefetch?
anika: Yep, yesterday we bumped prefetch_factor to 8 and increased batch_window_ms to 200 in continuous-batching config to improve throughput for long sequences.
jamie: That correlates — mixed long/short workload causes long requests to hold batch packs; with high prefetch we’re filling KV cache with large prefixes.
sre-oncall: Customer impact: three enterprise tenants (svc-finance, svc-search, svc-docs) reported degraded performance. No data plane errors, but timeouts/retries increased. CS looped in.
customer-success: We’ve contacted the impacted accounts, they are affected but not fully severed. They want ETA for mitigation.
mike: Hypothesis: prefetch_factor*batch_window increased packing of long sequences causing starvation for short ones, continuous batching kept aggregating large KV entries -> cache blowup -> paging -> disk stalls -> scheduler slowdown.
anika: Agreed. Immediate mitigation options: 1) revert prefetch_factor to 2, 2) reduce batch_window_ms to 50, 3) enable short-request prioritization in scheduler, 4) cap per-connection pack_size.
sre-oncall: Prioritize low-risk config changes first. I’ll push caps and reduce batch_window. Tara, can you prepare a rollback of prefetch change if needed?
tara: Will do. Preparing rollout plan.
deploy-bot: Deploy request queued by sre-oncall: config/continuous-batching -> set batch_window_ms=50, pack_size_cap=16, enable fairness=true. Reviewing canaries.
jamie: Also set kv_prefetch_size_limit=64MB to prevent unbounded prefetch.
sre-oncall: Rolling to canaries in us-west-1 (10% traffic) now.
(2m later)
deploy-bot: Canary deploy successful. No immediate regressions. Monitoring.
mike: Early signs: p99 down to ~1.1s, error rate trending down. KV cache growth slowed.
anika: Triggering scheduler fairness flag to prioritize short requests: `scheduler.mode = "hybrid_fair"`.
sre-oncall: Applied scheduler change to primary clusters. Observe for queuing oscillations.
(5m later)
jamie: Tail latency back near baseline for most tenants. Affected enterprise tenants reporting improved response times.
customer-success: Customers acknowledged improvement, asking for root-cause and next steps.
sre-oncall: Current mitigation: batch_window reduced, pack_size capped, scheduler set to hybrid_fair. Prefetch remains at 8 for now; plan to revert if stable but we should be cautious.
tara: I’ve prepared a rollback patch for prefetch_factor to 2 if we see recurrence. Will only roll if metrics re-worsen after 30m.
mike: Quick note for post-incident: add tests for mixed-shape workloads in CI e2e — ensure long requests don’t starve short ones.
anika: Opening follow-up items: (1) permanent scheduler change evaluation, (2) tighten default prefetch limits, (3) KV cache eviction safeguards and monitoring alert thresholds, (4) run replayed workload to reproduce.
sre-oncall: Creating incident ticket and linking to this thread. Severity: Sev2. Will draft customer-facing summary.
customer-success: Please cc me on communications.
jamie: Also assign an infra engineer to investigate pack allocation heuristics.
sre-oncall: Assigning to @mike and @tara for hotfix/rollback plan. Ops: continue monitoring for 60m.
(30m later)
mike: Metrics steady. p99 ~900ms, errors back to baseline. KV cache stable. No further paging observed.
anika: Good. We’ll keep fairness on and leave pack cap for 24h before rollback.
sre-oncall: Postmortem owners: anika (lead), jamie (scheduler), tara (deployment), mike (kv). ETA draft: 48h.
incident-bot: Incident updated: state -> mitigation in place. Incident channel created: #incident-2387654321 (auto).
customer-success: Sending customers a short update: ETA for full RCA 48h, mitigation applied, next update in 24h.
sre-oncall: Great. Any other asks? Otherwise closing paging/ops loop and moving to follow-ups. :thumbsup:
